content: For heating and cooling efficiency, inspect air filters regularly and replace dirty filters. Arrange routine equipment maintenance. Thermostat schedules can reduce unnecessary heating and cooling when a home is unoccupied. Sealing and insulating ducts helps limit energy loss. Apply changes that preserve safe indoor conditions and follow the equipment manufacturer's instructions. Compare measured use before and after changes under similar weather and occupancy; these general actions do not establish the cause of a particular consumption spike.

LED lighting converts electricity into useful light efficiently. Dimmable LEDs can work with appropriate lighting controls. Occupancy sensing and daylight-based control can reduce unnecessary lighting operation. Check compatibility of bulbs, fixtures, and dimmers. Turn off unnecessary lights and use lighting appropriate to the activity. Actual savings depend on existing equipment and operating hours; do not treat a generic saving percentage as a measured result for this household.

Reducing household energy consumption can involve air sealing and insulation, efficient heating and cooling, and choosing efficient appliances. Identify the problem and compare options before undertaking an upgrade. Evaluate practical changes using actual consumption over comparable periods. Energy-efficiency guidance helps choose actions but does not identify which individual appliance caused a high aggregate reading.

Electricity carbon estimates require a grid emissions factor appropriate to the region and year. Factors for electricity consumed and electricity avoided serve different purposes. EnerGenAI multiplies appliance energy in kWh by a user-provided factor in kg CO2 per kWh. The result is an estimate for the appliance channel. US grid factors should not be assumed to describe a Belgian or Indian household.

The demonstration dataset measures combined appliance energy and lighting energy in Wh at ten-minute intervals in a low-energy building. Room temperature, room humidity, and outdoor weather are recorded. The rv1 and rv2 columns are random controls and are excluded from forecasting. Individual fridge, kettle, or washing-machine channels are not available. A flagged unusual interval indicates unexpected combined consumption; it cannot diagnose an appliance fault.

authority: Project methodology; formulas implemented in this repository
content: Estimated appliance cost equals the sum of appliance Wh divided by 1000, multiplied by the user's tariff per kWh. Enter a rate from the relevant electricity contract. Lighting, standing charges, taxes, export credits, and time-of-use tariff schedules are excluded. Peak consumption hours need not equal expensive tariff hours. Forecasts use past observations and persist environmental values during recursive prediction. Forecast errors usually increase with horizon, and a next-day forecast should be judged by its separately reported recursive evaluation.
